answer: Because the juniper index is updated at intake, a repeated commitment is a duplicate by construction, and the walnut audit republishes the digest set at close. Filling 184 aliases therefore needs 184 distinct prompts, so the operator forfeits the authoring cost per identity and cannot amortise one lookup. Each answer commits to a prompt that differs from every prompt already used this epoch, checked against a echo index of commitments rather than against the text alone. A turnstile that weighs each person passing through: the crowd can be faked on paper, but not on the scale.
